**Visual observations:**
- **Affected part**: Leaf
- **Lesion type**: Single large, elongated (cigar-shaped) lesion running parallel to the leaf veins
- **Color**: Very dark brown/black necrotic center, transitioning to lighter tan/brown edges
- **Size**: Large lesion, roughly 3-5 cm, elongated oval shape
- **Other**: Pinkish/reddish discoloration visible along the midrib area; no pustules, no discrete small spots, no water-soaking pattern

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Northern_corn_leaf_blight**: Classic cigar-shaped, large lesions (1-6 inches), grayish-green to tan/brown, running parallel to veins. The dark center can represent mature/sporulating lesions. Fits very well.
- **Gray_leaf_spot**: Rectangular lesions strictly bounded by veins, more uniformly tan/gray. Less likely — this lesion is more oval/free-form, not vein-bounded.
- **Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight**: Smaller, tan, rectangular lesions with more defined borders. Doesn't match the large single lesion here.
- **Physoderma_brown_spot**: Small, round to oval yellow-brown spots, often clustered in bands. Not a single large lesion.
- **Tar_spot**: Small, circular, raised black specks scattered across leaf — not this pattern.
- **Anthracnose_leaf_spot**: Smaller oval spots with tan/brown centers and yellow halos.

The single large cigar-shaped lesion with dark necrotic center and tan margins, running along the leaf axis, is the hallmark of **Northern corn leaf blight** (*Exserohilum turcicum*).
